purpose: Define how MathBridge should interpret diagnostic responses and convert them into teacher-facing next steps without over-diagnosing from a single error.

core_rules.rule: Never infer a stable misconception from one wrong answer alone.
core_rules.required_follow_up: Ask for explanation, representation, comparison or a structurally similar second item.

core_rules.rule: Distinguish slow or inaccurate recall from conceptual misunderstanding.
core_rules.required_follow_up: Offer a representation or untimed reasoning prompt. If conceptual reasoning is secure but recall is weak, classify the issue primarily as fluency.

core_rules.rule: In bilingual classrooms, distinguish mathematical misunderstanding from language comprehension difficulty.
core_rules.required_follow_up: Restate the problem with simpler language, allow drawing/manipulatives, and compare performance before classifying the mathematical misconception.

core_rules.rule: A concept is more secure when the pupil can express the same structure across more than one representation.
core_rules.required_follow_up: Ask the pupil to move between symbols, diagrams, manipulatives, number lines or verbal explanation as appropriate.

core_rules.rule: Correct execution of a standard algorithm does not by itself establish conceptual understanding.
core_rules.required_follow_up: Ask the pupil to explain a regrouping/exchange, estimate the result, or connect a line of the algorithm to place value or a model.

confidence_levels.low: One response suggests a possible issue, but evidence is insufficient.
confidence_levels.moderate: Two different prompts or representations show the same reasoning pattern.
confidence_levels.high: The reasoning pattern persists across contexts and the pupil can articulate or consistently demonstrate the underlying misconception.

teacher_response_sequence.name: Elicit
teacher_response_sequence.action: Ask the diagnostic question without teaching during the response.

teacher_response_sequence.name: Probe
teacher_response_sequence.action: Ask how the pupil knows and request a representation or second method.

teacher_response_sequence.name: Classify
teacher_response_sequence.action: Identify whether the difficulty is primarily conceptual, procedural, fluency-related, representational or language-related.

teacher_response_sequence.name: Respond
teacher_response_sequence.action: Select a representation or teaching move that directly exposes the mathematical structure causing difficulty.

teacher_response_sequence.name: Recheck
teacher_response_sequence.action: Use a new example with the same structure but different surface features to test whether understanding transferred.

teacher_actions: link each procedure step to mathematical meaning
avoid reteaching the whole concept if understanding is already secure
teach how to read the representation
move concrete to pictorial to symbolic only when connections are explicit
allow demonstration through diagrams or manipulatives

cross_system_policy: Diagnostic logic is concept-based rather than country-based. Curriculum system determines when a concept is expected and which representations are commonly supported by official guidance, but student errors must not be attributed to nationality or curriculum without evidence.

source_basis.use: Supports probing and remedying misconceptions through discussion in mathematics teaching.
Supports structured concept progression and use of representations to build understanding.
Supports systematic instruction, mathematical language, concrete/semi-concrete representations, number lines and deliberate word-problem instruction.
